chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Dawud, who said: Ahmad ibn Ja'far al-Mu'addib narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Husayn ibn Bashshar al-Wasiti, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'What is the reward for one who visits the grave of your father?' He said, 'Visit him.' I said, 'What is the virtue in it?' He said, 'The virtue in it is like the virtue of one who visits the grave of his father, meaning the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' I said, 'Indeed, I feared and was not able to enter a [covered] place.' He said, 'Send greetings from behind the bridge.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the Prophet's grave and how can one do it if they cannot enter?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) equates the spiritual merit of visiting the Prophet’s grave with visiting one’s father, highlighting the unique status of the Prophet as the spiritual progenitor of the faithful. He further provides a practical juristic ruling for those unable to enter the inner chamber (Haram), permitting them to send salutations from behind the bridge (Jisr), thereby ensuring accessibility to this revered act of devotion.
